# 4 Sampling theory

## Tutorial 6, Exercise 9
```{r}
# Population parameters
N <- 3000
mu <- 68.0
sigma <- 3.0
```

### 1. With Replacement

* **The mean of the sampling distribution of the sample mean** is always the po

$$
\mu_{\bar{x}} = \mu = 68.0
$$
$$
\sigma_{\bar{x}} = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}} = 6.0
$$

### 2. Without Replacement

$$
\sigma_{\bar{x}} = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}} \sqrt{\frac{N-n}{N-1}}
$$


### 1. 

```{r}
n <- 25
sigma <- 0.6
mu <- 68

# X \sim N(68, 0.6^2)
z1 <- (66.8 - mu) / sigma
z2 <- (68.3 - mu) / sigma
z3 <- (66.4 - mu) / sigma

prob1 <- pnorm(66.8, mean = mu, sd = sigma)
prob2 <- pnorm(68.3, mean = mu, sd = sigma)
prob3 <- pnorm(66.4, mean = mu, sd = sigma)

cat("1. Probability is: ", prob2 - prob1)
cat("Expected number of samples: ", mu * (prob2-prob1))

cat("2. Probability is: ", prob3)
cat("Expected number of samples: ", mu * prob3)
```

## Tutorial 7

```{r}
n <- 120
p <- 0.5
#  Apply theorem
mu <- n * p
sigma <- sqrt(n * p * (1 - p))

z1 <- (47.5 - mu) / sigma
z2 <- (72.5 - mu) / sigma
prob1 <- pnorm(z2) - pnorm(z1)
z3 <- (74.5 - mu) / sigma
prob2 <- pnorm(z3, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("1. 40%-60% with approximation:", prob1, "\n")
cat("2. > 5/8 with approximation:", prob2, "\n")
```

## Exercise 10

```{r}
n <- 400
p <- 0.02
mu <- n * p           # 8
sigma <- sqrt(n * p * (1 - p))  # 2.8

z1 <- (11.5 - mu) / sigma
prob1 <- pnorm(z1, lower.tail = FALSE)

z2 <- (8.5 - mu) / sigma
prob2 <- pnorm(z2)

cat("1. > 3%:", prob1, "\n")
cat("2. < 2%:", prob2, "\n")
```

## Distribution of Diffs

## Tutorial 8

```{r}
mu_A <- 1400
sigma_A <- 200
mu_B <- 1200
sigma_B <- 100
n <- 125

mu_diff <- mu_A - mu_B  # 200
sigma_diff <- sqrt((sigma_A^2 / n) + (sigma_B^2 / n)) # 20

z1 <- (160 - mu_diff) / sigma_diff
prob1 <- pnorm(z1, lower.tail = FALSE)

z2 <- (250 - mu_diff) / sigma_diff
prob2 <- pnorm(z2, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("1. More than 160h:", prob1, "\n")
cat("2. More than 250", prob2, "\n")
```

## Exercise 11

```{r}
n <- 1000
mu_single <- 0.50
sigma_single <- 0.02

mu_diff <- 0
var_total <- n * (sigma_single^2) # 0.4
sigma_diff <- sqrt(var_total + var_total) # sqrt(0.8)

# |diff| > 2
# Synmetric
z <- (2 - mu_diff) / sigma_diff
prob <- 2 * pnorm(z, lower.tail = FALSE)

cat("Answer:", prob, "\n")
```
